items.info: Center Pedestal. Both levers in the CUT OFF detent before any power goes on.
items.label: Thrust Levers

items.info: Overhead Panel. One switch powers up the aircraft and its screens. Press the rightmost MFD button to clear the splash screen. The screens drain the battery quickly: if External Power shows AVAIL, press it to connect ground power until the generators come on.
items.label: Battery

items.info: Center Pedestal. Prevents the aircraft from rolling during prep. Chocks and covers can only be shown with it set and the engines off.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Controls the seat belt and no-smoking illumination in the passenger cabin.
items.label: Passenger Signs

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Displays the current total fuel weight onboard to verify it matches the flight profile requirements.
items.label: Fuel Quantity

items.info: Center Pedestal, right touchscreen (GTC2): Home > Utilities > Initialization. Press Preflight on the System Tests page to run the fire, stall and switch-light tests, enter weight and fuel (Get from Sim fills it in), enter V1, VR and V2 and press All On, then go Back and press Accept Initialization.
items.label: Avionics Init

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Initializes the flight management system with departure, arrival, route, and performance parameters.
items.label: FMS

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD). Sets the local barometric altimeter pressure reference on the flight displays.
items.label: Baro Reference

items.info: Instrument Panel. Verifies that airspeed reference bugs and flight display configurations are correctly selected for departure.
items.label: Bugs / PFD / MFD

items.info: Side Console. Tests the cockpit crew oxygen supply pressure and integrated microphone communications.
items.label: Oxygen Mask

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Confirms via the status synoptic page that the main entry airstair and baggage doors are closed and latched.
items.label: Doors

items.info: Center Pedestal, right touchscreen (GTC2): Home > Aircraft Systems > System Controls > Exterior Lights. In NORM the aircraft runs each light itself: nav and logo with power on, beacon with an engine running, taxi light above 5 kt on the ground, landing lights and strobes on the runway or with the gear down in flight, recognition lights below 18,000 ft.
items.label: Exterior Lights

items.info: Center Pedestal. Start with the right engine. Drag its lever from CUT OFF to the IDLE detent with the mouse (click spot just above the pedestal switches): joystick and keyboard throttles do nothing while a lever is in CUT OFF. Don't use the sim's Ctrl+E auto-start, which fights the levers.
items.label: Thrust Levers

items.info: Instrument Panel. Press the start button for the engine just set to IDLE; it lights green and the FADEC runs the start. The engine display shows STARTER, then IGN, with START in cyan. ITT should rise within 15 seconds and must stay below 556°C; the starter drops out at 45% N2. The engine is running in about 20 seconds at about 23% N1 and 52% N2. Then set the left lever to IDLE and press the left start button.
items.label: Start Button

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Monitors key parameters including N1, N2, ITT, and fuel flow to verify normal engine light-off.
items.label: Engine Instruments

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Confirms that both generators have automatically come online and bus voltages are normal.
items.label: Electrical Panel

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Sets the environmental control systems to automatic and enters the destination field elevation.
items.label: Bleed & Pressurization

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Controls the engine inlet, wing leading edge, and windshield anti-ice heating elements.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Yoke and Rudder Pedals. Verifies full, free, and unobstructed travel of the ailerons, elevator, and rudder surfaces.
items.label: Flight Controls

items.info: Center Pedestal. Takeoff flaps are the TO/APPR detent. The lever has three positions: UP, TO/APPR and LDG.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Yoke and Center Pedestal. Positions the pitch, roll, and yaw trims within their specified takeoff ranges.
items.label: Trims

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD/MFD). Verifies that the Crew Alerting System is clear of any unexpected warning or caution messages.
items.label: CAS & Messages

items.info: Center Pedestal. Release before taxi. The aircraft needs about 40% N1 to start rolling.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Rudder Pedals. Tests the primary toe brakes and confirms responsive tracking of the nosewheel steering system.
items.label: Brakes & Steering

items.info: Center Pedestal. Double-checks that the flap lever position and display indications match the planned takeoff setting.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Yoke and Center Pedestal. Final check to ensure pitch, roll, and yaw trims remain properly adjusted for departure.
items.label: Trims

items.info: Center Pedestal. Confirms that the speed brake switch is retracted and the tail spoiler surfaces are fully stowed.
items.label: Speed Brakes

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD/MFD). Performs a final scan of the Crew Alerting System display prior to entering the runway.
items.label: CAS & Messages

items.info: Thrust lever handle, side button. Press TO/GA: the flight director holds 11° nose up and wings level, and green TO shows for both modes on the PFD. Follow it on the takeoff. Check the heading, speed (V2 + 10) and altitude bugs.
items.label: Flight Guidance

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Verifies that passenger signs are active and the cabin is secured for departure.
items.label: Passenger Signs

items.info: Center Pedestal, left touchscreen (GTC1). Enter the squawk code, then press the XPDR1 mode button above it and select TA ONLY. This aircraft has no RA mode: TA ONLY reports altitude and adds traffic advisories.
items.label: Transponder

items.info: Center Pedestal, left touchscreen (GTC1): Home > Weather Selection > WX Radar Settings. Turn the radar on and set the display to Weather. Home > Map returns to the map view.
items.label: Weather Radar

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Confirms the required engine and airframe anti-ice systems are active based on local icing conditions.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Center Pedestal. Hold the toe brakes, push both levers to the TO detent and let the FADEC set takeoff thrust. Check N1 is within 1% of the target, then release the brakes. Takeoff thrust is limited to 5 minutes.
items.label: Thrust Levers

items.info: Yoke. Applies smooth aft pressure at rotation speed to establish the initial climb pitch attitude.
items.label: Rotate

items.info: Instrument Panel. Raises the landing gear handle after confirming a positive rate of vertical speed on the instruments.
items.label: Positive Climb

items.info: Center Pedestal. Retract once clear of obstacles and at no less than 130 KIAS.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Verifies that all landing gear have fully retracted and all gear doors are closed.
items.label: Landing Gear

items.info: Glareshield (autopilot panel), YD button. Damps out yaw oscillation, the side-to-side wallow, for a steadier ride.
items.label: Yaw Damper

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Confirms on the display that the wing flap surfaces have fully retracted.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Center Pedestal. Pull both levers back to the MCT detent passing 1,500 ft above the airport, then lower the nose to accelerate to 210 KIAS. Takeoff thrust is limited to 5 minutes. With the E2 autothrottle armed, selecting FLC does this for you.
items.label: Thrust Levers

items.info: Glareshield (autopilot panel). Press AP, then FLC with the speed bug at 210 KIAS, then NAV to follow the flight plan up to cruise altitude.
items.label: Autopilot

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Monitors outside air temperature and visible moisture to adjust anti-ice settings during the climb.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD). Passing the transition altitude (18,000 ft in the US), press the baro knob to set standard pressure, 29.92 inHg.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Turns off the seat belt sign once the aircraft is established in smooth air during the climb.
items.label: Passenger Signs

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD). Cross-checks the primary altimeter displays to ensure they show the identical standard flight level.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Scans engine operating data to verify normal performance and fuel burn rates at cruise altitude.
items.label: Engine Instruments

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Monitors fuel remaining and checks tank balancing against flight planning values.
items.label: Fuel Quantity

items.info: Instrument Panel (MFD). Verifies that cabin altitude, pressure differential, and outflow valve scheduling are normal.
items.label: Pressurization

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Illuminates the passenger seat belt signs to secure the cabin before leaving cruise altitude.
items.label: Passenger Signs

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Inputs the reference approach airspeeds and planned landing flap settings into the FMS.
items.label: Landing Data

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Inputs the destination field elevation to schedule automatic cabin depressurization for landing.
items.label: Pressurization

items.info: Flight Deck. Completes the review of the arrival procedure, approach charts, landing minimums, and taxi routing.
items.label: Approach Briefing

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Activates structural and engine anti-ice systems if icing conditions are anticipated during descent.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Glareshield (autopilot panel), ALT SEL knob. About a minute before top of descent, when the vertical deviation scale appears next to the altimeter, set the first altitude constraint.
items.label: Altitude Selector

items.info: Glareshield (autopilot panel). Press VNV: a yellow light under the button and a white VNV on the PFD show it is armed, and it turns green when the descent starts at top of descent. Outside E2 mode there is no autothrottle, so hold about 55–60% N1 and watch the speed.
items.label: VNAV

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD). Switches the altimeter reference from standard pressure to local station setting when passing the transition level.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD). Re-verifies that both the pilot and copilot altimeters are set to the current local barometric pressure.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Confirms that the cabin is fully secured and all passenger seat belts are fastened for landing.
items.label: Passenger Signs

items.info: Instrument Panel (PFD/MFD). Conducts a final scan of the Crew Alerting System to ensure no active faults exist.
items.label: CAS & Messages

items.info: Center Pedestal. Approaching the initial approach fix, slow to about 180 KIAS and select TO/APPR (limit 200 KIAS).
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Glareshield (autopilot panel). At the initial approach fix, press the Active NAV softkey below the PFD to change the navigation source from FMS to LOC, then press APR. The PFD shows LOC, then a green GS when the glideslope is captured.
items.label: Approach Mode

items.info: Instrument Panel. Lowers the landing gear handle and verifies three green down-and-locked indicators.
items.label: Landing Gear

items.info: Center Pedestal. Re-verifies that speed brakes are stowed to ensure normal lift profiles and handling on touchdown.
items.label: Speed Brakes

items.info: Center Pedestal. Select LDG once the gear is down and the speed is below 160 KIAS, then fly the approach speed (Vapp). Stay at TO/APPR if there is any ice on the airframe.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Verifies that required anti-ice systems are active or adjusted for the runway environment.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Yoke, left side. Press the red disconnect button by minimums (200 ft above the runway on an ILS). In E2 mode, disconnect the autothrottle too.
items.label: Autopilot

items.info: Center Pedestal. At 50 ft above the runway, bring both levers smoothly to IDLE and touch down with a small flare.
items.label: Thrust Levers

items.info: Center Pedestal. After touchdown, lower the nose, extend the speed brakes and brake until below 40 kt. In E2 mode they deploy on their own at touchdown.
items.label: Speed Brakes

items.info: Center Pedestal. Verifies that the speed brake switch is retracted after completing the landing rollout.
items.label: Speed Brakes

items.info: Center Pedestal. Retracts the wing flaps fully to the up position to prevent damage from ground debris during taxi.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Yoke and Center Pedestal. Set the pitch trim back in the green band, ready for the next takeoff.
items.label: Trims

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Turns off all structural and engine anti-ice heating elements after taxiing off the runway.
items.label: Ice Protection

items.info: Center Pedestal, right touchscreen (GTC2): Home > Aircraft Systems > System Controls > Exterior Lights. Left in NORM, the taxi light runs on its own. On dark or wet taxiways, the recognition and landing lights can be switched ON to add light.
items.label: Exterior Lights

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Switches the weather radar and traffic alerting system to standby upon clearing the runway.
items.label: Radar & TCAS

items.info: Center Pedestal. Sets the parking brake handle to secure the aircraft once stationed at the parking ramp.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Center Pedestal. Pulls both levers fully aft into the cutoff gate to shut off fuel and initiate engine shutdown.
items.label: Thrust Levers

items.info: Center Pedestal (GTC). Turns off the passenger signs to allow deplaning once the aircraft is safely parked.
items.label: Passenger Signs

items.info: Cabin. Open the main entry door to allow passengers to deplane after the aircraft is fully secured.
items.label: Cabin Door

items.info: Overhead Panel. Switches the single battery off and powers down the aircraft. Open the doors first: they only work with the engines off. Switch and load positions carry over to the next flight.
items.label: Battery

description: Instantly distinctive for its over-wing engine mounts, offering maximized cabin space and cutting-edge aerodynamics.
